speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Works as an elementary school teacher. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Patient
text: Alert and active. No head injury, abdominal pain, or chest pain reported. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Acute appendicitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: I must clarify that while appendicitis causes pain, the mechanism of a rear-end collision with abnormal leg positioning strongly suggests an orthopedic injury like a hip or pelvic fracture. Can you tell me if the pain radiates down your leg or if you feel any numbness? REQUEST TEST: X-ray_pelvis_and_femur. REQUEST IMAGES for the X-ray results.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pelvic_X-ray findings indicate no fractures in the pelvic ring or femoral neck, but the alignment suggests a posterior dislocation of the right hip.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Hip Posterior Dislocation. Based on the X-ray confirming posterior dislocation without pelvic fractures, your leg being held in an internally rotated, adducted, and flexed position is classic for this injury, which requires immediate closed reduction.
